rows.name: level_timer_digits (TIME)
rows.notes: World 1-1 level timer shown as TIME. Encoding: three bytes, each holding one decimal digit 0-9 (not packed): $07F8 = hundreds (0 during play), $07F9 = tens, $07FA = ones. Differential search: snapshot s0->s1 (16 'decreased' survivors) showed $07F9 7->6 and $07FA 5->3, i.e. displayed TIME 075 -> 063 (-12 counts). A 300-frame play_input/watch on $07F8-$07FB showed $07F9 stepping 9->8 and $07FA stepping 8,7,6,...,0 then wrapping to 9 with $07F9 borrowing (98,97,...,90,89...), one step about every 24 frames (~0.4 s), while $07F8 stayed 0. Proof by write: while the HUD read TIME 085, write_memory $07F8-$07FA = 0,9,9; the game's own next decrement redrew the HUD and the screenshot showed TIME 097 (RAM 0,9,7), i.e. the display followed the written value and counted down from it. Source: differential search.

rows.name: level_timer_digits (TIME)
rows.notes: World 1-1 level timer shown as TIME. Encoding: three bytes, each a single decimal digit 0-9 (not packed BCD): $07F8 = hundreds (stays 0 during a level), $07F9 = tens, $07FA = ones; the value decrements with borrow. Differential search: s0->s1 'decreased' left 16 candidates including $07F9 7->6 and $07FA 5->3, i.e. TIME 075 -> 063 (-12 counts). A 300-frame play_input/watch on $07F8-$07FB showed $07F9 stepping 9->8 and $07FA stepping 8,7,...,0 then wrapping to 9 with a borrow from $07F9 (98,97,...,90,89...), one step ~24 frames (~0.4s), $07F8 pinned at 0. Proof by write: with the HUD reading TIME 085, write_memory $07F8=$00,$07F9=$09,$07FA=$09 (099); the game's next decrement redrew the HUD and the screenshot showed TIME 097 matching RAM 0,9,7. Source: differential search.

rows.name: coin_count_digits
rows.notes: Coin count shown next to the coin icon in the SMB HUD. Stored as two decimal digits, one per byte, at $07ED (tens) and $07EE (ones); the display redraws only when a coin is taken. Differential search: coin grabbed in 1-1 (score +200, coin x00 -> x01) gave d2 (332 'increased' survivors); a second coin after a death narrowed it, and intersecting with the 'new value = 1' set left 5 candidates for the ones digit, with the increase to 2 on the second coin leaving $07EE alone at a plausible low address. Proof by write: (a) with the HUD at x02, write_memory $07EE=$07 made the next coin show x08; (b) write_memory $07EE=$10 (16) then a coin: the increment routine added 1 in the ones byte, normalised 17>=10 to ones 7, tens+1, so RAM read $07ED=1,$07EE=7 and the screenshot showed the HUD coin count x17. The tens byte only moves on the 9->10 rollover, so the first differentials did not see it. Source: differential search.

rows.name: score_digits
rows.notes: Six-digit score (plus a fixed 0 ones tile) shown under MARIO. Differential search + write proof. After a coin (+200 from 000000): c0->c1 'increased' left 332 candidates; a second coin (+200 from 000200 -> 000400) and filtering to values that went with the score left $07E1 (and $07DB) as the hundreds digit; only the hundreds digit changes for +200. Proof by write: while the HUD read 000400, write_memory $07E1=$09; collecting a coin (+200) redrew the HUD as 001100 (900+200), proving $07E1 = hundreds. Extent proof: wrote $07DD..$07E2 = 1,2,3,4,5,6 and one byte before it ($07DC=0); collecting a mushroom (+1000) changed $07E0 from 4 to 5 (RAM read 1,2,3,5,5,6) and the screenshot showed MARIO 1235560, so $07DD is the displayed leading digit and $07E0 the thousands digit; $07DC is not part of the score (the leading digit shown was 1, not 0). $07E3 read 0 throughout. Source: differential search. (A companion byte $07DB tracked the score in both coin events too; not recorded here.)
